title: The Volatility Apocalypse - Systematic Investor 303

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/The Volatility Apocalypse - Systematic Investor 303.docx

speakers: Cham (guest, volatility and options market-structure strategist; name garbled in captions)
summary: July 2024 Systematic Investor. Guest argues vol supply from structured products and zero-DTE options pins the index, creating record dispersion and making breadth a poor short-term signal; sets a calendar path for Aug-Sep vol, the US election, steepener, Europe and long-dated gold calls.

coverage.note: intro, sponsor, trend index returns, record dispersion
vol supply pins index, single-stock vol higher, 2017 analogy
zero DTE, structured products, XIV unwind, concentrated positioning
1997 analog, FX carry, yen, breadth meaning
breadth as long-term fragility, Nvidia Taiwan coin flip
gamma and call speculation, reflexivity in momentum
counterintuitive endings, calendar effects, wealth effect
wealth effect and collateral, seasonal path 2024
August-September vol calendar trade, warning shot
path to early next year, signature of vol unpinning, election start
Nixon-China analogy, Biden replacement discussion (political, no method beyond note)
election vol, year-end flows, Trump trades, 10y 5%
Fed chair, steepener, Olympics, Europe catch-up
French bank buy, contrarian conditions, structured products in Europe
US vs Europe wobble, gold calls, debt

completeness_estimate: 0.75 - the first reader caught the main vol-supply, 0DTE, breadth, calendar-path, populism, Trump-trade and gold-call ideas; it missed many supporting mechanisms (index-to-constituent causality, why structured products grew, dealer hedging loop, reflexive liquidity), several caveats and the Biden-replacement and Europe sub-arguments.

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: we're seeing record dispersion uh what do I mean by record dispersion you're seeing four times the volatility of the constituents um uh relative to the indexes themselves
claims.claim: In summer 2024 equity dispersion is at a record: constituent volatility is about four times index volatility, off the chart in 150 years of history, and this has broken the breadth signal.
claims.indicator: constituent volatility vs index volatility; breadth
claims.testable: yes: dispersion and correlation are measurable

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: the amount amount of structured product issuance and the amount of vol Supply at the
claims.claim: Heavy structured-product issuance and index volatility selling (vol supply) pin the index, and by arbitrage constraints this raises single-stock volatility and lowers correlation, because idiosyncratic moves must be offset to hold the index flat.
claims.indicator: structured product issuance, index vol supply, implied correlation
claims.direction: dispersion up, correlation down, index calm
claims.testable: partly: vol supply is hard to measure directly

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: index fall Supply means the market is going to have a very hard time breaking down uh and anytime quickly think 2017 right
claims.claim: Index vol supply means the market has a hard time breaking down soon, similar to 2017 when there was no pullback larger than 50bp for about two months; the same structural flow gives the same outcome.
claims.indicator: size of index pullbacks; vol supply

correction.issue: Misstates which period had no pullback: Cham says the market has now (summer 2024) gone almost two months without a pullback greater than 50bp, and that this looks very similar to 2017 because the same structural effects cause the same outcome. The claim instead dates the two-month stretch to 2017.
correction.fix: Cham: heavy index vol supply means the market will find it very hard to break down any time soon; the S&P has not had a pullback larger than 50bp in almost two months, which resembles 2017, because the same structural flows are producing the same outcome.

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: we have the uh the increase of zero DTE option uh trading that is uh not a on its own a uh a v Supply it can be the opposite it can also unpin markets
claims.claim: Zero-DTE option trading magnifies gamma pinning when structured products have already loaded dealers with gamma, because speculators sell zero-DTE for quick profit, which reflexively adds gamma and more pinning; it can also unpin markets.

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: eventually it won't end well but but it took a year and a half of record low realiz volatility record correlation breakdowns and incredible profits in law selling
claims.claim: Volatility-selling regimes can last 1.5 years with record-low realized volatility before a violent unwind (Volmageddon / XIV in 2017-18); the regime can continue six more months but hedging the tail is valuable.
claims.testable: yes: study short-vol regime lengths and unwinds

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: a concentrated positioning somewhere in the market uh generally uh that's a liquid XIV would be a perfect example right
claims.claim: Sharp breaks need concentrated positioning in an illiquid vehicle or entity (XIV) that cannot be absorbed; the next break will probably involve zero-DTE hedging by a stressed fund.
claims.testable: no: concentration is hard to observe

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: you need a macro event to kind of lead but that will cause stress and the key is that causing enough stress in some
claims.claim: A macro shock (like the 1997 Asian crisis and dollar/China link leading to LTCM) must stress a concentrated entity to break the vol-supply regime; large FX carry trades, with dollar-yen above 160, are a candidate trigger.

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: everything goes really slowly and then breaks all at once right
claims.claim: Fragile structures sit stable and then break all at once, with vol supply holding everything together in the meantime.

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: it no longer is relevant over a one week one month one quarter period it it could be relevant over a one year twoyear uh period
claims.claim: Market breadth stays informative about medium-to-long-term fragility (1-2 years) but is no longer a reliable trading signal over weeks to a quarter, because structural vol flows now dominate.
claims.testable: yes: test breadth signal at several horizons

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: this is a coin flip that something's going to happen here and the next next two three years
claims.claim: Nvidia, now the biggest company, is the epicenter of a Taiwan risk judged by the guest as a coin flip over two to three years, which could cause a 30% market downturn, so narrow breadth creates fragility.

correction.issue: Attribution of the probability: the coin-flip estimate for something happening over the next two to three years is presented by Cham as what people in the US government and others in the know say, which he adopts; the claim presents it as his own independent judgement. The 30% downturn is his estimate.
correction.fix: Cham: Nvidia, now the biggest company, was the epicentre of the Taiwan fear in 2022, and people in the US government and others in the know see roughly a coin flip that something happens in the next two to three years; with Nvidia at the centre, such an event could cause about a 30% market downturn, which is how narrow breadth matters.

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: you have uh negative gamma in those names you have positive gamma on the index and in the meantime you have short interest in those names and all kinds of things that are just squeezing it higher
claims.claim: Single-stock call speculation leaves dealers short gamma while index vol selling leaves them long gamma, so mega-cap names get squeezed up while the index stays pinned, as when Nvidia rose 10% on earnings with the index flat.
claims.indicator: single-stock call buying, dealer gamma, short interest

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: it's all about reflexivity I mean you and I briefly talked about this before but you know it's not just the wealth effect it's um it's a liquidity effect you know a market break necessitates a further Market break
claims.claim: Momentum ends through reflexivity and often counterintuitively: if small caps rally while the index is pinned, mega-caps must fall, calls stop paying, call volume turns to selling and momentum reverses.
claims.testable: partly: reflexive chain hard to test

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: markets going down uh will lead to a worse outcome and and markets going down don't necessarily happen as a function of bad news uh they happen as a function of a change in underlying positioning
claims.claim: Market declines often start from changes in underlying positioning rather than bad news, and market strength can itself change positioning and end a trend.

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: there's things that happen just based on uh broad events that just exist not because the election is per se a bad thing for markets
claims.claim: Calendar effects come from liquidity and option-expiry mechanics: vol supply dissipates and risk rises as summer holidays end and approaching events such as elections need hedging, so seasonality has structural causes.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne (host)
claims.quote: the market being a more important leading indicator for the economy than the economy been a leading indicator for the market
claims.claim: Rising asset values and the wealth effect make the stock market a more important leading indicator for the economy than the reverse.

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: we have $75 trillion of new asset value and people like well wait why does that matter because that's what collaterals those are collateral you've just increased the amount of actual dollars the whole system
claims.claim: Global equity gains of about 25% on roughly $300 trillion of equity-linked assets create about $75 trillion of new collateral and effective money supply, so the wealth effect is a large stimulus whose reversal would force deleveraging.
claims.indicator: global asset value change as collateral
claims.testable: partly: collateral multiplier hard to measure

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: coming out of February of this year like if we didn't see a little wobble in February this year it was risk on for the year
claims.claim: Seasonal and options-expiry structure plus election-year fiscal and monetary liquidity support markets: if no wobble came in February 2024 the year would be risk-on, with a slow grind and dispersion in the summer.
claims.indicator: opex dates, vol supply, liquidity injections

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: the best trade going forward here is actually not just selling Ball but buying calendars going out and buying longer dated ball to sell shorter dated ball
claims.claim: Trade a calendar spread: buy longer-dated volatility (30-90 day VIX futures) and sell shorter-dated, because short-term vol stays well supplied while long-dated vol should rise into the August 14 VIX expiry, September opex and November election.
claims.indicator: VIX term structure, 30-90 day implied vol
claims.direction: long back-end vol, short front-end vol

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: when that ball starts to unpin I think it's going to happen on the upside
claims.claim: When vol supply unpins, volatility rises first with a faster move up (mini blow-off top) and a warning-shot pullback of maybe 10%, followed by a year-end rally, not an immediate crash.
claims.direction: vol up with market up first

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: you generally see a unpinning of that index fall a a a increase that broadly allows then for movement in the market and something bigger to come down the road
claims.claim: Before a bigger decline, one usually sees an increase in index volatility unpinning the market (a warning shot); this pattern is based on 25 years of experience.
claims.testable: yes: check vol rise precedes drawdowns

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: the millennial generation on down who is becoming increasingly uh dominant in politics um are populist why because they were at the bottom part of the distribution
claims.claim: Millennial-and-younger voters are populist because they lost out to asset inflation; this drives anti-incumbent votes, protectionism and inflation (a flat tax), as in the 1964-82 period, and will persist for years.

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: it took somebody like Nixon to go open up China because people saw him as you know Hardline anti- you know protectionist
claims.claim: Policy outcomes are counterintuitive: just as Nixon opened China, Trump may make a deal with China; the initial protectionist or inflationary tariff trade may be right at first but should not be overextended.

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: people have gotten very burned you know the collective memory over the last two elections right um uh is that Vault was high and it
claims.claim: Because implied volatility around the last two elections was a buy, nobody wants to sell election vol; the guest expects a volatile but mean-reverting outcome where sellers and buyers both struggle and the market goes nowhere over a month.

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: end of year flows and a year that market is up 25% or very positive
claims.claim: After a 25% equity year, annual rebalancing and reinvestment (about 10% of $75 trillion, roughly $7.5 trillion) concentrates at the start of the next year, so people front-run year-end flows and early next year flows become important.
claims.direction: buy into year end, flows early next year
claims.testable: partly: flow size is an estimate

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: I think we're going to hit 5% again in the 10e uh before the end of the year
claims.claim: Playing a Trump win: expect a yield steepener, gold higher and volatility up, with the 10-year back to 5% by year end.
claims.direction: steepener: short-term rates lower, long-term higher

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: I don't think Powell is long for this world once Trump is a
claims.claim: A Trump administration would run the economy hot with a Fed chair change (like Nixon and Burns), pricing higher inflation and a steepener, a trade not heavily positioned.

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: election years Olympic years that that 3-week uh period is one of the least volatile
claims.claim: The three-week Olympics period in election years has historically been one of the least volatile, because liquidity and volume-weighted time are low.
claims.indicator: volatility during Olympic period; volume-weighted time
claims.testable: yes: event study on Olympics periods

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: I think Europe could play a little bit of a catch-up trade
claims.claim: Europe may catch up to the US into year end because cheap energy (LNG) and near-shoring help Germany and weak sentiment is overdone.

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: you don't play many rsion um in all markets right that'll get you into trouble but you know when the when the the the rhetoric is so negative
claims.claim: Contrarian mean-reversion trades should not be played in all markets, but when rhetoric is very negative and positioning one-sided (France after the snap election, as with China), a real inflection and bigger bull move can follow.

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: in terms of Demand by markets it's actually quite strong in Europe the difference though is increasingly these products are tied to the S&P 500
claims.claim: European structured-product demand is strong but increasingly tied to the S&P 500, so the vol-supply effects are centred in the US.

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: a wobble in August September if it happens with all going higher ironically could hit the US worse than somewhere like Europe
claims.claim: A wobble in the pinned US market could hit the US harder than Europe, and Europe could outperform from there, giving a change of trend.
claims.direction: long Europe versus US into a wobble

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: the trade in gold in the next decade is long long painted calls
claims.claim: Own long-dated gold calls for ten years because implied vol was low and realized vol rises in structurally inflationary, protectionist, populist periods; the 1968-82 episode saw dramatic vol in bonds, FX and gold.

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: US debt is to a point right where it's unsustainable
claims.claim: Unsustainable US debt is likely to end in the Fed buying debt, which is inflationary; in the 1971 analog the dollar initially fell but gold was the primary beneficiary.

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: you hold that long dated call position and after you get a dramatic volatile move right you may W to sell some short dated strangles against it to fund it
claims.claim: Hold long-dated gold calls and trade around them: sell short-dated strangles after big moves to fund decay, and buy calendar call spreads; gold's bull trend should not be hit by an equity wobble and would gain from higher equity vol.
claims.indicator: gold calls, short-dated strangles, calendar call spreads
claims.testable: yes: option structure can be backtested

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne (host)
claims.quote: ongoing weakness in the end uh certainly one of the key drivers there and also obviously the the equity Market rally continuing bonds quite choppy
claims.claim: In early July 2024 SG Trend was +0.66% and SG CTA +0.54% month to date (CTA +7.81% YTD; the Trend YTD figure is garbled in the captions), driven mainly by continued yen weakness and the equity rally while bonds were choppy.
claims.indicator: SG Trend, SG CTA indices; USDJPY trend; equity trend

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne (host)
claims.quote: trade in the markets it obviously worked very well 2022 uh and being kind of long the uh constituent Ball versus short index fall
claims.claim: The dispersion trade (long constituent volatility versus short index volatility) became popular and worked very well in 2022, which frames the question of why dispersion is returning in summer 2024.
claims.indicator: single-stock implied vol vs index implied vol (dispersion trade)
claims.direction: long constituent vol, short index vol
claims.testable: yes - dispersion trade P&L from implied vol and correlation data

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: the constituents uh follow the path of the index and the index is driving uh a significant amount of the flows
claims.claim: Causality runs more than ever from the index to its constituents rather than from constituents up to the index: index-level flows (structured products, passive, vol supply) drive the single-stock path, contrary to the natural bottom-up view.
claims.indicator: index-level flows and positioning vs constituent returns
claims.conditions: heavy index-level products and passive flows
claims.testable: partly - lead-lag between index flows and constituent returns

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: do I want to be betting on a 10% perom outcome from here uh in stocks when I can do that easily with interest rates higher right with Structured Products
claims.claim: Structured-product issuance has surged for about 2.5 years because, after the weak 2022 and with high rates and high valuations, banks can offer a defined roughly 10% outcome far more attractively than outright stock exposure, which creates the index vol supply.
claims.indicator: structured product issuance; interest rate level
claims.testable: yes - issuance data vs index implied vol

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne (host)
claims.quote: they sell when the index goes up the buy when it goes down that pins it that encourages more volatil selling and it feeds on itself
claims.claim: Dealers long gamma from vol sellers hedge by selling index strength and buying weakness, which pins the index, rewards further volatility selling and makes the process self-reinforcing.
claims.testable: yes - dealer gamma estimates vs realized index range

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: that's what he does and I've talked to him a decent amount about this and and that's his biggest position
claims.claim: David Dredge, a specialist in Asian FX, holds the possible break of the yen/Asia carry trade as his biggest position, and the guest agrees that this is among the most likely sparks for the vol-supply regime to break.
claims.conditions: dollar-yen above 160, high leverage in carry
claims.testable: partly - carry unwind episodes can be studied, specific timing cannot

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: structure product issuance is like this is not levered and it's distributed across all kinds of Institutions
claims.claim: Structured-product vol supply is unlevered and spread across many institutions, unlike concentrated vehicles such as XIV, so when the regime breaks it will not be the cause, although unwinds can still cause pain as with Chinese snowball contracts.
claims.testable: partly - leverage and concentration of holders are hard to measure

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: we don't talk about it as much because you know we've forgotten about what's happening Russia Ukraine we kind of we get bored of some of these macro stories
claims.claim: Markets get bored of macro tail risks such as a Taiwan conflict even though their probability has not changed, so complacency grows while Nvidia, once left for dead on that fear in 2022, becomes the biggest company.
claims.conditions: geopolitical tail risk concentrated in one large stock

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: there's a natural market Machinery that will just continue to push that in line um or push that out of line until the impetus come
claims.claim: Breadth-related fragility needs a catalyst to resolve; until then call buying, short interest, passive investment and momentum effects keep pushing the mega-cap names higher, so the structure can persist.
claims.indicator: short interest, passive flows, call volume in mega-caps
claims.conditions: negative gamma in single names, positive gamma at index
claims.testable: partly - persistence of squeezes is testable, catalyst timing is not

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne (host)
claims.quote: these flows are short-term indicators but if the short-term indicators lead to path that then breaks you know leads the actual long-term outcomes
claims.claim: Short-term flow indicators must be monitored because they steer the path that eventually breaks and determines long-term outcomes; ignoring them while watching only macro news misses the big picture.
claims.testable: partly - value of flow indicators over fundamentals is testable

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: it's priced very steeply so you're gonna have to sell a low ball to buy a high ball it'll still supply and demand matters more than any of the theoretical realities there
claims.claim: The vol calendar is already priced steeply (sell low-dated vol, buy high-dated vol) but the guest still prefers it because supply and demand in the vol market matter more than theoretical fair value.
claims.direction: long back-end vol, short front-end vol
claims.conditions: front-end vol well supplied; steep term structure
claims.testable: yes - calendar spread P&L vs term-structure slope

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: usually that first wobble you know uh especially if people are expecting it or talking about it right it's going to be hard for it to uh really break things
claims.claim: A widely expected and discussed first wobble rarely breaks the market, since positioning has adapted, so the initial pullback is likely a buyable warning shot rather than the main decline.
claims.conditions: wobble that is anticipated and discussed
claims.testable: partly - could test pullbacks after high attention vs low attention

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: I think early next year we could see some real second move fireworks
claims.claim: After the year-end rally, a vol-up market should make volatility more unpinned and unstable, with a larger second move expected in early 2025.
claims.conditions: vol supply unpinning after year-end rally

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: have to measure as we go and see how the characteristics change and what that means for the path of outcomes
claims.claim: The multi-step scenario path (moves one to five) is the most likely path but conditional: it must be re-measured as market characteristics change rather than followed as a fixed forecast.
claims.conditions: path updated as vol supply and market characteristics change

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: they are up from 40% of wealth creation in household formation to 45% the last two years
claims.claim: Millennials have risen from about 40% to 45% of household formation (wealth creation) in two years and gain share every four years as baby boomers die off, which sets a long timeline for the populist, anti-incumbent political shift.

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: I think there's enough doubt as to whether he he will still be present that it's not too late to to make some of those trades
claims.claim: Because the market still doubts that Biden remains the Democratic candidate, it is not too late to position for a Trump win (steepener, gold, vol); this is like buying out-of-the-money puts, with the risk of buy-the-rumour-sell-the-news into the election.
claims.indicator: Trump-win pricing in rates, gold, vol
claims.direction: long steepener, gold, vol for Trump win

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: the only uh person that he can hand that to legally um in in a transfer would be his vice president Kamal haris and and she is incredibly unpopular
claims.claim: Replacing Biden is structurally hard: his roughly $100 million of campaign funds can legally pass only to Vice President Harris, who is unpopular, and party-base constraints rule out most alternatives, so the window is narrow and the same Trump-favoured outcome likely stays.

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: the seasonality into Thanksgiving and Christmas that could cause the final push end of year um higher in markets
claims.claim: After election-related volatility, seasonality into Thanksgiving and Christmas should deliver a final push higher into year end.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne (host)
claims.quote: they have been a little bit better than expected but unemployment rates ticked up so the bonds haven't really gone anywhere dramatically
claims.claim: After the debate the Trump trade lifted yields for a few days, but payrolls beat while unemployment ticked up, so bonds had not moved decisively and a Trump win was not obviously priced in.
claims.indicator: US Treasury yields after June 2024 debate; payrolls and unemployment rate

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: given the Vol Supply given the placidity that's here and that the low probability of some stressful event coming out of there
claims.claim: With heavy vol supply and market placidity, the French election is seen as a short-term trade with a low probability of a stressful event and outcomes better than the market prices.
claims.indicator: French equities, OAT spreads around the snap election
claims.testable: yes - French equity returns after the July 2024 election

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: I was out there publicly talking about buying BMP with two hands into this recent pullback
claims.claim: The guest bought BNP Paribas (caption: BMP) aggressively into the French pullback, citing a top-tier global bank with business lines in positive secular trends, as a concrete use of the contrarian-reversion idea.
claims.indicator: BNP Paribas after French election pullback
claims.conditions: July 2024, negative rhetoric and one-sided positioning

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne (host)
claims.quote: the banks tend to hold sovereign debt so if you get a wobble like this they uh tend to get hit on the double
claims.claim: European banks hold sovereign debt, so political stress hits bank equities twice (directly and via sovereign bond losses on their balance sheets); the ECB has tools to intervene but signals it will let markets play out.
claims.indicator: bank equities vs sovereign spreads; ECB intervention tools
claims.direction: banks fall when sovereign yields rise

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne (host)
claims.quote: the changes were seeing in international Reserve managers and their Holdings of dollars and treasuries and shifting more into gold
claims.claim: International reserve managers are shifting from dollars and Treasuries towards gold, which supports gold structurally alongside dollar-role and global fragmentation arguments.
claims.indicator: central bank gold reserves vs USD and Treasury holdings
claims.testable: yes - IMF COFER and central bank gold purchase data

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: it's not one world connected it's a bunch of different areas competing against each other both in
claims.claim: A fragmented world of competing blocs and economic warfare creates massive flows and realized volatility in bonds, FX, dollar and gold, and gold is the biggest beneficiary, as in the 1968-82 period.
claims.indicator: realized volatility of bonds, FX, gold in populist/protectionist regimes

claims.speaker: Cham (guest)
claims.quote: we have defined a very clear channel in Gold uh that we've just bounced off the bottom end of it
claims.claim: Gold has traced a clear price channel and has just bounced off its lower end, supporting buying calendar call spreads now within the longer-term bull trend.
claims.testable: yes - channel-bounce rule can be backtested
